messages:
ben: Customer reported failing CI for a Go module after a v2 release. CI error shows '401 Unauthorized' from the proxy and 'unknown revision v2.0.0' from go get.

sam: Which customer and repo? Any repro steps yet?

ben: AcmePayments, private org. They use GOPROXY=proxy.company.com in CI. Locally they had `replace github.com/acme/llm-go => ../local/llm` during development. On CI they expect to pull the tagged release. Root go.mod in the published artifact is `module github.com/acme/llm-go` (no /v2) but the git tag is `v2.0.0` (annotated).

julia: That screams module path vs semver mismatch. If you cut a v2 release Go modules expect the module path to include `/v2` when the major is bumped.

ben: Customer CI logs (sanitized):
```
go: finding module for package github.com/acme/llm-go
http: 401 Unauthorized
go: github.com/acme/llm-go@v2.0.0: reading github.com/acme/llm-go/go.mod at revision v2.0.0: unknown revision v2.0.0
```

eli: The 401 suggests proxy auth for a private module, but the 'unknown revision' part means the proxy couldn't find a matching module info for that tag. If go.mod inside the tag doesn't align with the module path the proxy may reject it or index it incorrectly.

sam: Customer mentioned their release job runs `git tag` and `git push --tags` after CI. Could the release packaging step have left the old module path because the dev `replace` hid the change locally?

julia: Best repro we ask them to run:
1) GOPROXY=direct GOSUMDB=off go get github.com/acme/llm-go@v2.0.0
2) git ls-remote --tags <repo-url>
3) curl the module archive from the registry and `tar -tf` then `cat` the go.mod in the archive to check the `module` line

ben: I ran step 1 against our staging proxy and saw the same behavior. `git ls-remote` shows the v2.0.0 tag exists. Inspecting the tarball in registry shows go.mod with `module github.com/acme/llm-go` (no /v2).

eli: Root cause (likely): upstream bumped the tag to v2.x but did not update the module path in go.mod to `github.com/acme/llm-go/v2`. Fix options:
  - Proper fix: update module to `module github.com/acme/llm-go/v2`, bump minor/patch, re-tag (v2.0.1) and republish.
  - Alternative (not recommended long-term): keep module path as v1 style and avoid v2 tag (but that breaks semver expectations).

sam: Short-term workaround for the customer?

julia: They can bypass our proxy and pull directly from VCS: `GOPROXY=direct GOSUMDB=off go get github.com/acme/llm-go@v2.0.0` — that fetches the tag straight from git and sidesteps the proxy 401, but it doesn't solve the semantic mismatch and will complicate CI reproducibility.

ben: Is there any registry-side mitigation? Can we rewrite module paths on ingest or map tags to module paths?

eli: Registry team responded: we currently index based on module path inside go.mod. If the go.mod doesn't include /v2 but tag is v2, the indexer marks it inconsistent. We flagged the package and asked upstream to republish. We can't safely rewrite module path because imports would break downstream users.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-5483 — module-path-semver-mismatch (support escalation). Assigned to @julia and @eli :rotating_light:

sam: Logging KB draft: "Go module v2 tag exists but module path lacks /v2 — causes unknown revision / proxy 401 in private GOPROXY setups." Include steps: git ls-remote, fetch tarball, check go.mod, and recommended upstream fix.

ben: I opened the escalation with Acme and shared the exact repro steps and logs. I'll update the customer with the direct-get workaround and ETA for upstream republish. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
